summary.en: Kenyan-led forces and Erik Prince's contractors are now using drones and air support to strike gang positions in Port-au-Prince and Kenscoff, while Sri Lankan police, army and a Bangladesh UN advance team have been deployed to Haiti. The United Nations has renewed sanctions on Haiti and allocated US$75 million for life-saving aid to 507,000 people. Four soldiers from the UN-backed force and five Salvadoran soldiers remain missing after a gang ambush, showing continued threats to foreign troops. President Bukele has threatened Haitian gangs over the abduction of Salvadoran soldiers and launched a military operation to rescue them. The conflict caused 193 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Kenyan-led forces og Erik Princes entreprenører bruker nå droner og luftstøtte for å angripe gjengposisjoner i Port-au-Prince og Kenscoff, mens srilankanske politiet, hæren og et bangladeshisk FN-fremrykkende team er blitt utplassert til Haiti. De forente nasjoner har fornyet sanksjoner mot Haiti og avsatt US$75 million til livredende hjelp til 507 000 personer. Fire soldater fra den FN-støttede styrken og fem salvadoranske soldater er fortsatt savnet etter et gjengeoverfall, noe som viser vedvarende trusler mot utenlandske tropper. President Bukele har truet haitiske gjenger over bortføringen av salvadoranske soldater og igangsatt en militæroperasjon for å redde dem. Konflikten forårsaket 193 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Haitian conflict
background.extract: Since 2020, Haiti's capital Port-au-Prince has been the site of an ongoing armed conflict between rival gangs and the state. The government of Haiti and national security forces have struggled to maintain their control of Port-au-Prince amid this conflict, with gangs speculated to control up to 90% of the city by 2023. In response to the escalating fighting, an armed vigilante movement, known as bwa kale, also emerged, with the purpose of fighting the gangs. On 2 October 2023, United Nations Security Council Resolution 2699 was approved, authorizing a Kenya-led "multinational security support mission" to Haiti. Until 2024, the war was between two major groups and their allies: the Revolutionary Forces of the G9 Family and Allies and the G-Pèp. However, in February 2024 the two rival groups united in a coalition known as Viv Ansanm, formed to oppose the government and the UN mission.
